# HEMS Workshop — Harsh-Environment Mass Spectrometry
> 25+ years of scientific proceedings on mass spectrometry for space, underwater, field-deployable, and defense applications.

## About
The HEMS Workshop is a biennial scientific conference focused on mass spectrometers designed for extreme operational environments: planetary exploration (Mars, Titan, Europa), underwater oceanography, battlefield chemical detection, environmental monitoring, and industrial process control. Founded in 1999, the workshop series brings together researchers from NASA, ESA, military laboratories, and academic institutions.

## Workshop Archives
Each archive page contains: full technical program with session schedules, downloadable presentation PDFs, abstract PDFs, author/institution lists, corporate sponsor information, and student award winners.

### Machine & AI Ingestion Interface
To allow AI search agents, academic citation scrapers, and custom models to map and digest the entire HEMS body of work with zero HTML scraping overhead, a flat machine-readable proceedings database is served at:
- [/archives-index.json](file:///archives-index.json): Full flat array of all 436 historical presentations, posters, and abstracts (including authors lists, affiliated institutions, workshop years, session titles, presentation slides PDF links, and abstract PDF coordinates).

## Key Topics
Portable mass spectrometers, miniaturized instruments, ion trap technology, time-of-flight MS, membrane inlet mass spectrometry (MIMS), MALDI-TOF, quadrupole mass filters, coded aperture design, chemical warfare agent detection, planetary surface analysis, spacecraft atmosphere monitoring, underwater dissolved gas analysis, differential mobility spectrometry, field-deployable GC-MS

## Content Types
- Technical presentations (PDF slides)
- Extended abstracts (PDF)
- Poster session materials
- Student award presentations
- Corporate sponsor directory
- Workshop programs and participant lists
